stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 7 inactives: Kelce active for Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 7 Buzz

Week 7 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 7

Biggest concerns ahead of Sunday
Players in Paris
ACTIVE

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints (back): Kamara has been a mainstay on the Saints' injury report for weeks but has not missed time. In fact, he was removed from the team's final injury report, meaning he is active for Week 7. Still, New Orleans has also been using Kendre Miller and sprinkling in CJ Donaldson as well. Miller is the preferred option here, but even he is just a volume RB2/flex play for managers in need.

Rico Dowdle, RB, Steelers: He has been limited at practice this week but is active for Week 7. Dowdle saw 28% of the team's snaps last week, with seven carries and four targets, going for 7.9 fantasy points. He is more of an insurance back than a standalone option at this point. Regardless, Jaylen Warren remains a strong start.

Players with early starts
ACTIVE

Rashod Bateman, WR, Ravens (shoulder): He practiced in full this week and was not on the final injury report. He is active for Week 7. Still, after leaving early last week, there is more risk than usual with Bateman. For example, we have seen Buffalo's DJ Moore exit early multiple times this season because of his shoulder injury. Bateman is a boom-or-bust deeper-league flex option. Lane is the preferred play out of the Ravens' WR options. However, without Lamar Jackson under center, fantasy managers should look elsewhere if possible.

Quinshon Judkins, RB, Browns (ankle): Judkins is active for Week 7. Consider him to be an upside RB2 against a Titans defense that has allowed 99 RB rushing yards per game. Game script should also be on Cleveland's side, which means added volume. Dylan Sampson, who has been activated off the IR, should be the No. 2 RB. He's worth an add in deeper leagues.

Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (foot): The breakout rookie is active for Week 7. He put up only 15 yards last week, but the Titans rank in the top 10 in WR fantasy PPG allowed. Consider him to be a boom-or-bust WR3/flex option this week.

KC Concepcion, WR, Browns (calf/quad): The rookie is active for Week 7. His usage has been increasing, but the production is not enough to start him outside of the deepest of leagues. For the time being, he remains more of an upside stash.

Dalton Schultz, TE, Texans (quad): Schultz missed practice to start the week, but is active for Week 7. With the Texans having more receiving options -- Marvin Harrison Jr., a surging Jaylin Noel and Tank Dell returning -- volume has been less safe for Schultz. That was his fantasy appeal. I would go with the other streaming options listed in this article over him.

Jordan Mason, RB, Vikings (thumb): Mason is active and will return to action in Week 7. He has played in only one game this season, but out-snapped Aaron Jones Sr. 29-26 in that contest. Mason had 15 carries to Jones' 12, but both had one goal-line TD. I would expect Mason to have the slight edge in ground work, while Jones should handle more in the passing game. Both are in play as flex options against the Colts, who have allowed the seventh-most RB fantasy PPG. Game script should be on their side this week as well.

Adonai Mitchell, WR, Jets (finger): He practiced in a limited fashion this week and is active against the Dolphins. Mitchell had 12 targets in the last game before his injury. He's worth grabbing off the waiver wire in deeper leagues. However, Omar Cooper Jr. is coming off a big game, and the two will be competing for playing time and targets behind Garrett Wilson. With Mitchell returning, it makes Cooper more of a boom-or-bust option this week. That said, Cooper is the preferred option of the two.

Baker Mayfield, QB, Buccaneers (thumb): It was a bit surprising when Mayfield returned to practice this week. In fact, he is active for Week 7. Still, this is more of a boost for Tampa Bay's pass catchers; I'd recommend taking a "wait and see" approach with Mayfield. Some options to play instead include C.J. Stroud and Aaron Rodgers.

Bucky Irving, RB, Buccaneers (illness): Irving has been limited at practice but was removed from the final report and is active for Week 7. He will be a strong start against the Panthers, who have allowed the third-most rushing TDs and fifth-most fantasy PPG to RBs. I would rank him as an RB1 for Week 7.

INACTIVE

Breece Hall, RB, Jets (ankle): Hall returned to the practice field Thursday and Friday, albeit in limited fashion. He is out for Week 7. Braelon Allen -- who has dominated volume with Hall sidelined -- should be started. The Dolphins have allowed the third-most RB fantasy PPG. They struggle against backs in the passing game, which means a bigger boost in PPR leagues. Plus, game script should be on the Jets' side in this one.

Tyjae Spears, RB, Titans (knee): Spears is out for Week 7. That means even more volume should go Tony Pollard's way. Pollard has seen at least 19 touches in three of his last four games. He is more of a "safe floor" play than an upside shot, but given how banged up the RB position is, it is worth getting him in lineups this week as an RB2 or flex option.

Players with late starts
ACTIVE

Jaylen Waddle, WR, Broncos (chest): Waddle has been limited in practice this week, is active for Week 7. He has surpassed 35 yards only once this season, but there's a chance here for a bounceback opportunity. He has a team-high 22% target share against zone, which the Cardinals play at the league's fourth-highest rate (87%).

Arizona has also allowed the sixth-most yards to WRs on deep passes, and Waddle leads the Broncos in deep targets. Lastly, the Cardinals have allowed the second-most TDs and seventh-most fantasy PPG to WRs. Waddle is in play as a WR3 with upside this week.

Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos (ankle): Denver's rookie RB practiced in full this week and is active on Sunday. However, Sean Payton indicated that he could be on a snap count in his first game back. Coleman should be added in any league in which he's available.

Despite wanting to roster him as much as possible, I recommend taking a "wait and see" approach before plugging him into lineups. J.K. Dobbins, who has had 18-plus touches in three of his past four games, is the preferred play in the Broncos backfield. Dobbins is an RB2 in a good matchup against the Cardinals, who have allowed the fourth-most RB rushing yards per game.

Josh Jacobs, RB, Packers: Jacobs is active for Week 7. He will be the lead back for the Packers, even if his workload is somewhat limited in his first game back with the team. The Lions are a tough matchup for RBs, but given the state of the position, Jacobs checks in as an RB2.

Christian Watson, WR, Packers (ankle): Watson is active for Week 7. Matthew Golden, who dealing with a shoulder injury, is active as well. Both are must-start options against the Lions, who have allowed the second-most WR fantasy PPG.

Puka Nacua, WR, Rams (calf):  Nacua left practice early Thursday and missed Friday, but is nevertheless active for Week 7. As such, he should be started in all fantasy leagues.

Players on Sunday night
Travis Kelce, TE, Chiefs (ankle): Kelce is active for Sunday Night Football. Kelce is a TE1 off volume alone, however, the Chiefs have been throwing less which has hurt his fantasy value. Start him, but expectations should be tempered against the Seahawks.

Players on Monday night
George Pickens, WR, Cowboys (shoulder): The star receiver was limited to start the week. It was his first time on the injury report this season. ESPN's Todd Archer notes that Pickens has had ice on his shoulder after the Cowboys' past two games. Still, Pickens said he will play in Week 7. Even in a tough matchup, you play Pickens.

Dallas Goedert, TE, Eagles (knee): The Eagles' tight end missed practice to start the week but was removed from the team's injury report on Saturday and should play in Week 7. He will likely be the top target for the Eagles, where volume alone should have Goedert in the TE1 range.

Saquon Barkley, RB, Eagles (hamstring): Barkley has returned to practice this week and is questionable for Week 7. If Barkley plays for the Eagles, he plays for fantasy managers. This is especially true against the Cowboys, who rank top seven in most RB yards and touchdowns allowed. Still, if Dameon Pierce is available on your league's waiver wire, it wouldn't be a bad idea to add him just to cover your bases with this being a Monday night affair.

Ruled out before Sunday
Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (ankle): Jackson is out for Week 7 after revealing that he had a high ankle sprain. Zay Flowers has averaged 10 targets per game with Tyler Huntley and has surpassed 12 fantasy points in each game. The ceiling is much lower without Jackson, but the floor is high enough to trust. The lack of Jackson takes a lot of the appeal away from Ja'Kobi Lane as a streaming option. I would look to avoid all Ravens outside of Flowers and Derrick Henry. Hunter is a superflex or streaming option for those needing to dive deeper.

Tyler Warren, TE, Colts: Warren is out for a second straight week. This should mean more volume for Keenan Allen and Josh Downs. However, the Colts have a very tough matchup against the Vikings, who have allowed the fifth-fewest WR fantasy PPG. Ideally, managers should look to avoid them both, but if you are in a pinch, volume can have them in play. Some replacement tight end options are Tyler Higbee, T.J. Hockenson, Michael Mayer, Juwan Johnson, Pat Freiermuth and Evan Engram.

Davante Adams, WR, Rams (hamstring): Adams will be out for six to 10 weeks. He can be safely added to IR spots in leagues that have them. Those that don't should still hold on to Adams, but dealing him (if you are in need of open bench spots) is also an option. I expect Konata Mumpfield to get the bulk of snaps opposite of Puka Nacua (if he plays), but the Rams will likely mix it up with their other wideouts. I want to roster Mumpfield, but not start him just yet. Terrance Ferguson is not expected to be back next week, but he remains a stash option I like, as he could be the team's No. 2 receiving option once he returns.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): The Eagles' WR1 has been ruled out for Week 7, as has his teammate WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). That leaves Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown and Darius Cooper as the Eagles' top receivers. They are purely options for those in deep leagues. That said, Cooper is the preferred play of the three, as he has the highest chance of scoring a touchdown.

Zach Charbonnet, RB, Seahawks (knee): Charbonnet returned to full practice this week but is out for Week 7. That will leave Emanuel Wilson as the lead runner once again. Volume has him as a flex option this week. However, it is a tough matchup against the Chiefs, who have allowed the second-fewest rushing YPG entering Week 7. Given the matchup, fantasy managers should try to avoid him if possible. Some options to play over him are Woody Marks, Ollie Gordon II, Jordan Mason and Bam Knight.

Mike Evans, WR, 49ers (Achilles): After leaving early on Monday night, Evans has not practiced this week and is out for Week 7. Deebo Samuel Sr. is also out for the Niners. That would make Christian Kirk (who practiced in full, is questionable and seems likely to make his 2026 debut) the 49ers' top receiver. Kirk would be in play as an upside flex option in 12-team leagues or deeper. The Falcons have allowed the sixth-most WR fantasy PPG.

Emeka Egbuka, WR, Buccaneers (concussion/foot): After Sunday's game, Egbuka developed concussion symptoms. He remains in the league's concussion protocol and is out for Week 7. That leaves Chris Godwin Jr. as the top target for Mayfield. Volume makes Godwin a flex option with upside, even in what appears on paper to be a tough matchup against Carolina. Ted Hurst III could get more usage and is a flier for those in really deep 12-team leagues.

stories.headline: Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick
stories.summary: Manchester United are weighing up replacements with Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
Manchester United are weighing up replacements with Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt, sources told ESPN.

United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to pile the pressure on Carrick.

It was the second damaging result in five days following a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

United have now gone eight games without a win in all competitions and sit 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation places.

Sources have told ESPN that the club are looking at replacements as they consider Carrick's position.

Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann -- both currently out of work -- are among the contenders.

Former Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna impressed in talks with United's hierarchy in the summer of 2024 before a decision was taken to retain Erik ten Hag.

Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, would be open to talks if contacted.

United, according to sources, spent time doing due diligence on a number of coaches before deciding to hand Carrick a two-year contract in May after the 45-year-old's successful interim spell.

It's understood there's a feeling internally that the club are prepared if Carrick is relieved of his duties.

Speaking after the defeat to Bournemouth, Carrick insisted he was in the dark about his future.

"I totally understand the situation," he said. "I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal."

stories.headline: Sixers overrule Embiid, sit center with plantar fasciitis management
stories.summary: Despite publicly calling to play Sunday against the Pistons, the 76ers decided to sit Joel Embiid due to right foot plantar fasciitis management.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- A day after Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid asked reporters to campaign for him to play in Sunday's game against Detroit -- the second of the Sixers' first back-to-back this season -- the 76ers ruled out Embiid for Sunday night's game against the Detroit Pistons with right foot plantar fasciitis management. ​

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them," Embiid said with a smile after Saturday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

Sixers second-year guard VJ Edgecombe was also ruled out for Sunday's game with an abdominal contusion.

The Sixers decided against Embiid's wishes, as they look to keep the former MVP healthy for a long season. Embiid, plagued by various injuries, has averaged just 49 games per season over his 10 years.

In their win over the Bucks on Saturday, Embiid had his tenth career triple-double, finishing with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Having him sidelined is a significant blow to the Sixers' already thin frontcourt.

Philadelphia also ruled out big men Dominick Barlow (back), Jabari Walker (knee) and Tacko Fall (quad). Walker injured his left knee in Saturday's win, exiting the game in the third quarter. That leaves Adem Bona as the team's only true center active on Sunday. Forward Dean Wade, who made his season debut on Saturday, will likely play some center, and LeBron James, who missed Saturday's game with sciatica management, has no injury designation and can also help out at the center spot.

The Pistons will be without All-NBA center Jalen Duren, who the team said has a hamstring injury and will be out for at least two weeks.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for first F1 title
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli produced another masterful drive to win the United States Grand Prix -- but will have to wait to clinch his first Formula 1 world title.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli produced another masterful drive to win the United States Grand Prix -- but will have to wait to clinch his first Formula 1 world title.

Antonelli came into the Austin, Texas, race with slim hopes of winning the championship with four races remaining, needing to win, for George Russell to finish ninth or lower, and for Lewis Hamilton fifth or lower.

While he held up his end of the bargain -- by more than 15 seconds from Charles Leclerc -- results elsewhere didn't quite go his way.

Hamilton extended the championship race by finishing fourth, and Russell just about did his bit despite managing only a disappointing eighth.

Antonelli will head to Mexico City next week with a whopping 123-point lead over Russell, with Hamilton a point further back. A placing of ninth or higher will seal the title no matter where his rivals finish.

He leaped from his Mercedes and launched himself into the arms of his mechanics for the ninth time in this dominant season.

Leclerc claimed second for a second successive week after an impressive race for Ferrari, making a late move on Max Verstappen, who completed the podium.

Lando Norris made a one-stop strategy work to claim fifth for McLaren.

Part 1 of Antonelli's job was done Saturday as he soared to a magnificent pole as the sun began to drop on the Circuit of the Americas. With Hamilton only fifth and Russell sixth, his chances of getting over the line increased.

If the Italian was feeling any nerves as he sat on the grid waiting for his shot at history, he certainly did not show them as he blasted off the line and left Verstappen in his wake.

The Dutchman was swallowed up by the fast-starting Leclerc, who also jumped Isack Hadjar. Verstappen then had to fend off Hamilton who rose to fourth. The Ferrari pair went wheel-to-wheel before Leclerc's magnificent move on Verstappen.

The four-time world champion was soon up to speed and rocketed up the inside of Leclerc to reclaim second, but Antonelli had already checked out -- 2.4 seconds ahead at the end of the opening lap.

Russell's role in the celebration-delaying picture was hampered as he was investigated for leaving the track and staying ahead of Oscar Piastri -- with whom he banged wheels as he rejoined.

A five-second penalty was dished out to the Mercedes man. In a race fraught with jeopardy, Russell and Hamilton were both on the cusp of handing Antonelli his crowning moment.

Verstappen was the first to pull the trigger on a pit stop on Lap 14, swiftly followed by Hamilton and Leclerc, but Antonelli -- who started on the more durable medium tires -- and Mercedes chose not to respond.

- Kimi Antonelli on brink of world title after win in Austin -- as it happened

- Kimi Antonelli ecstatic with first pole since July at United States GP: 'It's good to be back'

- Max Verstappen taking painkillers to deal with 'impossible' bumps at United States Grand Prix circuit

Russell pitted and served his penalty on Lap 24, rejoining a net eighth before Antonelli pitted a lap later and was now a net third -- on much fresher tires than those ahead.

New race leader Verstappen was showing strong pace, while Hamilton was promoted to fourth when Hadjar boxed.

The Dutchman pitted for a second time with 25 laps remaining as Antonelli charged through on Leclerc to lead once more.

Leclerc and Hamilton stopped again in the final 16 laps, rejoining at fourth and sixth -- with the British driver needing to make up two places to ensure he kept Antonelli from the trophy.

He dispatched Hadjar swiftly, but Norris had done a magnificent job on the one-stop strategy. The reigning champion -- about to yield his crown -- was reeled in on Lap 47 by Verstappen and Leclerc, and Hamilton rose to fourth the following lap.

All the action was taking place behind Antonelli, who marched on serenely out front.

"It was the result we needed," Antonelli said during the postrace interview. "The whole team deserve it so much. All this time putting so much work on bringing this new package and finally seeing the result is very pleasant.

"It was also perfect execution from strategy to call the one-stop. Really happy we made it stick. Today was a great team effort."

On his title hopes, he added: "We are very close. We try to finish on a high, and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Antonelli has been the standout of the 2026 season and, after fittingly shining brightest once again in the Lone Star State, will be crowned a worthy champion over the coming weeks.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Who I would -- and would not -- want to be this AFL offseason
stories.summary: The AFL offseason is in full swing but it won't stop us from analysing the landscape. Here's who Jake Michaels would (and wouldn't!) want to be heading into 2027.
stories.body:
From Brisbane's stunning three-peat to Fremantle's Grand Final capitulation, high-profile free agent signings to ongoing legal battles, so much has happened in the AFL world over the past month. So, who would you want to be (and not want to be) this off-season.

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Those I WOULD NOT want to be this AFL offseason
Ross Lyon
No coach will enter season 2027 under more scrutiny and pressure than Ross Lyon. St Kilda was widely tipped to rise up the ladder this season just gone after being the most active club during the previous trade and free agency period. Instead, the Saints severely underwhelmed, winning just 10 games and finishing a disappointing 11th on the ladder, 10 premiership points outside of the wildcard finals. The club is desperate to retain the services of superstar midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera, who is out of contract at season's end and could easily be tempted with a blockbuster move back to South Australia. As a result, St Kilda's powerbrokers likely won't tolerate another sluggish start, which means Lyon has absolutely zero margin for error in 2027.

Fremantle fans
Alright, alright, I'm sorry to bring it up again. And please feel free to skip ahead if you don't want to re-live it once more. But the reality is every single Dockers fan will be replaying those harrowing final four-and-a-bit minutes of the Grand Final in their mind all offseason, wondering how on earth their team coughed up what appeared to be an insurmountable late lead. The heartbreaking loss to Brisbane is as devastating as it gets for a footy club and you could almost understand if any Fremantle fan never wanted to watch the sport again. Seriously, I'm not sure how you ever get over that loss. It all just means the next five months are going to feel like an eternity.

Andrew McGrath
It was an incredibly disappointing season from new Essendon skipper Andrew McGrath, who averaged a career-low in disposals, kicked just two goals, and failed to poll a single Brownlow Medal vote. To be a captain of a club that won just two games for the entire year and still be unable to crack the top 10 of the best and fairest count is pretty embarrassing, really. With former skipper Zach Merrett now no longer at the club, McGrath, who has now been in the league for a decade and tallied 200 games, is Essendon's main man. It's time he starts to play like it or else he risks further damage to his reputation.

Chris Fagan's replacement
Whoever is entrusted with the task of succeeding Chris Fagan at the Lions will be feeling the pressure and the eyes of the footy world on them from day one. It's a bit like following Jerry Seinfeld on stage. How can you possibly back up that act!? Fagan completely revitalised Brisbane, leading the club out of the doldrums and to its second three-peat this century. And while Fagan's tenure is up and dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale has departed for Collingwood, nobody feels as if the Lions are over the hump. In fact, quite the contrary. The age profile of this list should have them contending for years to come. That can be both a blessing or a curse for any new coach.

The Pullman Five

Okay, this one might be a tad on the nose, but who would want to be one of Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice, or James Jordan this offseason? The incident at the Pullman Hotel in Melbourne on the eve of finals remains a legal matter, meaning there are still so many unknowns when it comes to the footballing careers of these five. Can Heeney and Warner ever ingratiate themselves to the Swans' faithful once more? Will Bice and Jordan be shuffled out of the best team? And then there's Blakey. North Melbourne gave up the farm for his signature and much will be expected of him at his new club. I'm just not sure he's the difference maker they think he is.

An (existing and competing) expansion club
At what point do we stop referring to Gold Coast and GWS as expansion clubs? Probably now. But I'm lumping them together in here for different reasons. The Suns were a total shambles this year, falling from flag favourite after three rounds to finishing in the bottom six and winning just two games after the mid-season byes. Spearhead Ben King has now departed the club and rumour has it Matt Rowell wants to follow suit. Damien Hardwick is under the pump and must show something in year four at the helm. Meanwhile, the Giants just held a fire sale, clearing out Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs. It's a bold move, and while it could pay dividends down the track, you figure there simply has to be some short term pain.

Those I WOULD want to be this AFL offseason
Zach Merrett
This time last year Merrett would have been top of my other list, but the veteran midfielder's wish of a fresh start at a new club has now been granted, and that must feel like an enormous weight has been lifted from his shoulders. Merrett joins the Hawks, a club which could easily have won the premiership this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's late heroics during preliminary final weekend. It means that for the first time in Merrett's career he will enter a season truly believing his side can go all the way. That's got to be a great feeling for an elite player who has toiled away for so long and enjoyed little success.

Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera
As we've established, his coach might be under immense pressure, but Wanganeen-Milera certainly shouldn't be feeling the pinch. In fact, he goes into next season with all options and possibilities on the table. If the Saints turn out to make good on their promise from last year and actually show they can compete with those at the pointy end, then he may well elect to sign on and remain at the club. But if 2027 turns out to be more of the same, he will have his choice of 17 new destinations to call home, including the two clubs from his home state of South Australia. Make no mistake, Wanganeen-Milera will be both the most discussed and in-demand player in the sport next season.

Andrew Mackie and Geelong's entire recruitment staff
When the siren sounded on the trade and free agency period, Geelong list boss Andrew Mackie should have been pumping his fists and popping bottles of champagne in celebration. The Cats have been arguably the biggest winners of the offseason to date, improving across every line with additions of former Giants captain Toby Greene, reliable ruck Rowan Marshall, and still criminally underrated key defender Jordan Ridley. It's a hefty haul and a great salvage after the club discovered at the eleventh hour it would be missing out on the services of Zak Butters. Mackie and his team have done their job, now it's over to Chris Scott and the playing group.

Fremantle fans
Alright, so there are the obvious reasons why you wouldn't want to be a Fremantle fan this offseason, but there are also plenty of reasons why you absolutely would. The Dockers came within an inch of winning their first premiership last month and proved to the footy world, and their supporters, the club has a list to not only go all the way in 2027 but remain one of the premier sides in the league for the next half decade. Just about everyone on this Fremantle squad is yet to hit their prime and has serious scope to improve next year. That should be both a worrying thought for the other 17 clubs and a great comfort to those who cheer for the men in purple.

Jason Horne-Francis
The departure of superstar midfielder Zak Butters during free agency means the keys to Port Adelaide now firmly belong to Horne-Francis. Some might argue he's shared those keys with Butters in recent years, but there's simply no denying who will be top dog at Port heading into next season. Horne-Francis is still just 23 years of age but he has shown he possesses all of the attributes to succeed as his club's main man. I expect him to relish the extra responsibility, too, and take his game to even greater heights. Jason, train hard and we'll see you in 2027!

Jaymie Graham
It must feel pretty special knowing a club made the decision to part ways with a four-time premiership-winning coach in favour of you, despite the fact you've never coached a senior AFL game. Graham arrives at Arden Street with an impressive resume as an assistant and has been tasked with ending North Melbourne's decade-long finals drought. Some will make the case he faces similar pressure to whoever takes over from Fagan at the Lions, but I see his role, at least in the immediate future, as one which carries far less of a burden. Given North's recent struggles, he will be offered (a little) time to get things right. His team is also in the sweet spot of being enough to win with now but not good enough to carry crazy expectation.

stories.headline: Lars Eller scores late goal as Panthers top Blackhawks 3-2
stories.summary: — Lars Eller's first goal of the season, with 2:23 left in the third period, lifted the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 win over the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — Lars Eller's first goal of the season, with 2:23 left in the third period, lifted the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 win over the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.


Eller beat Spencer Knight with a high shot just inside the left post as he raced down right wing and took advantage of Chicago line change. Matthew Tkachuk and Sandis Vilmanis also scored for Florida, which ended two-game losing streak.


Roman Kantserov and Ryan Greene connected for Chicago, which has dropped three straight.


Akira Schmid made 19 saves, while Knight stopped 29 shots.


The Blackhawks failed to score on seven power-play chances, including two brief 5-on-3 advantages, lowering their NHL-worst conversion rate to 8.33%.


Blackhawks defenseman Bowen Byram missed his fourth game with an upper-body injury. Kevin Korchinski, Chicago’s top pick in the 2022 draft, seventh overall, filled in and played his second game this season.


Florida forward Carter Verhaeghe played in his 500th NHL game and tallied an assist.


The Panthers outshot Chicago 15-6 in the first period and took a 2-1 lead.


Greene opened the scoring 2:34 in, getting just enough of a wobbling puck to direct it past Schmid after Korchinski’s shot from the point missed the net and bounced in front.


Vilmanis popped in a rebound of Sam Reinhart’s shot from a scramble to tie it at 6:49.


Tkachuk’s power-play goal, five seconds after Tyler Bertuzzi was sent off for tripping, gave Florida a 2-1 lead with 5:39 left in the first. Seth Jones’ shot from the point struck Tkachuk on the arm and bounded in.


Kantserov tied it at 2-2 at 11:15 of the second. He beat Schmid low on a screened shot from the right circle, capping a strong shift with linemates Patrick Kane and Connor Bedard.


Up next
Panthers: At Winnipeg on Tuesday in finale of four-game trip.


Blackhawks: Host Los Angeles on Tuesday to complete a seven-game homestand.


------

stories.headline: Time, place unclear for Game 6 of Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals
stories.summary: With the Valkyries forcing a Game 6 in the WNBA Finals, the Dream are working to resolve a scheduling issue that leaves the venue and time of the game up in the air.
stories.body:
After the Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday in Atlanta's State Farm Arena, tying the best-of-seven series at 2-2, one question was answered and another far more important question was raised.

There will be a Game 6 in Atlanta. But nobody knows where or even when the game will be played despite a furious round of negotiations spilling into Sunday between the WNBA, NBA, Valkyries, Dream and Atlanta Hawks, sources told ESPN.

The Dream -- whose home venue of Gateway Center Arena has a capacity of approximately 3,500 -- have played all five home playoff games at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, home to and operated by the Hawks. Coordination between the leagues, teams and multiple media partners resulted in Games 3 and 4 of the Finals getting moved to State Farm Arena. Game 3 was shifted up a day, from Thursday to Wednesday, while the Hawks agreed to hold a doubleheader with the Dream and moved tip time of Saturday evening's home opener back 30 minutes.

But with the Hawks hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm the night of Game 6, along with other scheduling complications, the situation is more complex than what the leagues dealt with earlier in the series and could have millions of dollars of impact on both leagues.

"We continue to explore all options," a WNBA spokesperson told ESPN.

Said a Dream spokesperson: "We are waiting to hear from the league if any changes can be made to allow us to play in State Farm Arena. If not, the game will be played in Gateway Center Arena."

Sources believe it's a real possibility that Game 6 will be held Thursday as scheduled at Gateway Center Arena in College Park.

"There are problems with all the solutions," one source close to the situation said.

Sources told ESPN that the NBA has been working with the Hawks and Cavaliers to determine if Thursday's game could be switched to an alternate date -- or even to Cleveland. While some stakeholders feel the onus should be on the NBA to move its regular-season game so the WNBA Finals can be prioritized, there has been pushback from others that the domino effects of moving that game are too complicated.

Thursday's Cavaliers-Hawks game is already a back-to-back for both teams: The Hawks host the Miami Heat at State Farm Arena on Wednesday, when the Cavaliers play a home game before traveling to Atlanta.

Moving Thursday's game to Cleveland is a radical idea that has been discussed, sources said, but it would create a home-road back-to-back for the Hawks in addition to the logistical nightmare of scheduling a new home game in Cleveland with just a few days' notice.

Following Thursday's game, Cleveland is supposed to play Saturday in Milwaukee, which could also be hosting Game 7 of the World Series. Fridays are NBA Cup exclusive games, while Hawks-Cavaliers is a non-Cup game.

State Farm Arena has open dates on Tuesday -- the day after Golden State hosts Game 5 -- and Friday. One proposal would move Game 6 of the WNBA Finals to Friday and Game 7, if necessary, from Saturday, Oct. 31, at Chase Center to Tuesday, Nov. 3.

The WNBA would support that proposal, but only if both teams agree to it, sources said.

The Valkyries have raised concerns about moving two WNBA Finals games and the three off days that proposal would create in between Games 5 and 6 as well as between Games 6 and 7, sources said.

"We're proud to be part of such a compelling Finals and love seeing the growth of the game," a Valkyries spokesperson said in a statement. "We fully support what's best for the league and will stand behind whatever it decides."

Playing Game 7 on Nov. 3 would conflict with a recent NBA policy of not holding games on Election Day, although sources said that does not currently appear to be a strong concern.

Availability at Chase Center is also not abundant. The Golden State Warriors -- whose ownership group also owns the Valkyries -- have home games scheduled against the LA Clippers on Sunday, Nov. 1, and Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2.

While they don't share an ownership group with the Dream, the Hawks have expressed a desire to help facilitate the WNBA Finals in their arena, as they did for Games 3 and 4, sources said. The Dream will be a full-time tenant at State Farm Arena beginning in 2027, the team announced earlier this month, which should make holding playoff dates in the future more seamless.

There has been discussion about moving Thursday's game to a matinee, like Game 4 was, sources said. The Hawks have been open to facilitating another doubleheader at State Farm Arena, but other sources said the WNBA believes the idea of a weekday matinee for a Finals game would not be as desirable compared to a weekend matinee.

Other Atlanta-area alternate arenas -- such as Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion or Gas South Arena in Duluth -- aren't viewed as ideal since they would feel like road games for both teams.

Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta sold out quickly once they were moved to State Farm Arena. Fans wanting to purchase tickets for Game 6 have been told to wait for a resolution to the scheduling conflicts, sources said.

While it is not uncommon for WNBA playoff games to be moved to alternate sites because of arena commitments to NBA games or other events, sources on all sides of this situation expressed frustration that these issues hadn't been resolved before Saturday.

"This should've been solved weeks ago, and definitely at the same time Games 3 and 4 were solved," one source said.

Said another: "The fact we are making these decisions so we can play a WNBA game at a larger arena is the best news of all. ... It just has to be scheduled better in advance. Moving games is much harder now than it would have been a week ago."

stories.headline: Who is this year's Mr. October? Tracking the playoff MVP for 2026
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players doing the most to help their teams win.
stories.body:
Who is hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we're tabulating the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But we've added a twist: The deeper we get into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carries. The division series counts double the wild-card round, then we'll double it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

This means that players who shine in the early rounds can still get on the leaderboard, but it's more difficult. Coming through when the championship leverage is at its highest is what becoming an October hero is all about.

Saturday's hero: Forget Sal Frelick's offensive numbers. The guy is a folk hero in Milwaukee. This was true before Saturday, but it's reached Bunyanesque proportions after Frelick smacked a game-tying homer in the sixth inning of Game 2. That evened the score at four and completed the Brewers' comeback from a four-run deficit. Frelick's fourth-inning single also contributed to the Brewers' third run. There were a lot of big momentum swings in Game 2, but nothing got the ballpark rocking like Frelick's blast.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cochrane set for Ipswich Jets
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

Oct. 23: Caleb Williams shows he is all the way back on TNF

By Adam Rank

There is going to be a lively debate between Chicago Bears and New England Patriots fans over the next number of years as to who got the better QB in the 2024 NFL draft. And, I hate to go all youth sports dad on you, but I'm just happy that both players are doing well.

And you should, too. Caleb Williams not only entered the NFL MVP conversation Thursday night, but he's a rock-solid starter for your fantasy team moving forward as well. This Bears offense has been on fire with Williams under center. The Bears have scored 120 points in the three games he has started and finished. He is just the third quarterback in Bears history with 300-plus passing yards and a win in back-to-back games, joining Billy Wade (1962) and Sid Luckman (1947). You can forgive Bears supporters for being a little excited about Caleb.

• You might remember when people were taunting Williams for being a checkdown merchant. Well, he had eight completions of 20-plus yards against the Patriots. That is tied for the most by a quarterback in a game this season.

• Luther Burden III has 250 yards after the catch this season, the second-highest total in the league behind Drake London (255). Burden finished the game with four receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. He wasn't the target leader, but Burden is the top wide receiver to trust for the Bears moving forward.

• Rome Odunze was clutch down the stretch for the Bears. Two big grabs on the final drive to set up the field goal that made it a two-score game. He also corralled the onside kick to seal the win. Great for the Bears. I'm not sure he's going to be somebody you can rely on week to week in fantasy. He's good for bye-week and injury replacement, but don't rush him into your lineups.

• Colston Loveland is a must-start every week. He had that brutal first game. He did nothing in the monsoon game, either. But Loveland has looked like the tight end you drafted in the two games since Caleb returned to the lineup. Is he going to score a touchdown every week? I hope, as a Bears supporter and dude who drafted a ton of Loveland. While not likely to score every week (I'm not ruling it out), he needs to be started.

• A.J. Brown had three receptions on six targets for 48 yards. Not great. But let him take this time on the mini-bye to get back into playing shape. He might even be a great candidate to trade for if you can convince some manager it's time to move on.

• Rhamondre Stevenson had a great fantasy night for you. Neither he nor TreVeyon Henderson were great at running the football, but Stevenson caught all five targets for 93 yards. Of course, a lot of it happened on a 48-yard reception at the end of the half. Not really sustainable, mind you. But it happened. The good news is the Patriots have the Dolphins next week, a team that has allowed the second-most fantasy points to running backs.

• Maye's 48-yard passing touchdown to Stevenson is the longest offensive touchdown to end a half since Jayden Daniels 52-yard desperation heave to Noah Brown in 2024. Both plays were against the Bears.

Lamar Jackson to be game-time decision

By Jamison Hensley, NFL Nation Ravens reporter

Baltimore Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is considered a game-time decision after being limited in practice all week with a sprained left ankle. Jackson had a noticeable limp while walking to the podium for his media session after Friday's practice. He said he feels he is "heading in the right direction" and the decision will come down to pain tolerance. "If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, that's not helping my team at all," Jackson said.

Cam Skattebo back in Giants' RB rotation

By Jordan Raanan, NFL Nation Giants reporter

Cam Skattebo is back in the New York Giants running back mix this week after receiving zero carries against the New Orleans Saints. Coach John Harbaugh said he had a "good week" of practice and that he was "always going to be a big part of our season." Skattebo was behind Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary in the running back rotation vs. New Orleans. Harris was cut earlier this week.

"I think I got taught a lesson," Skattebo said of the costly fumbles that landed him on the bench. Don't be surprised to see Skattebo and Tracy split most of the work in the Giants backfield this week against a tough Houston Texans run defense.

Oct. 22: Notable names you can bench in Week 7

By Michael F. Florio

Deciding whether or not to sit one of your big-name options is the toughest decision in fantasy football. Here are some big names you can consider sitting this week and some options you can start instead.

Patrick Mahomes has scored fewer than 18 fantasy points in three straight games, including just 10.5 last week. The Kansas City Chiefs rushing attack is so effective that it has hurt Mahomes' fantasy value, keeping him to 30 passes or fewer in the past three games. He also gets the Seattle Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest passing yards in the NFL. Sit Mahomes for the names listed above, as well as Tyler Shough and Aaron Rodgers. I would also sit Xavier Worthy.
Dak Prescott has scored fewer than 13 fantasy points in back-to-back games. Not only that, but he has topped 19 fantasy points only once this season, which came in a great matchup against the Washington Commanders. In each of the past four games he has just one touchdown. He faces the Philadelphia Eagles, who held him to one TD pass per game last season. This also could be a lower-scoring divisional matchup. I would sit him for Jordan Love, C.J. Stroud, Bryce Young and Kyler Murray if you have them.
While I do not think fantasy managers can sit them, I do want to warn that Chuba Hubbard and Ashton Jeanty could disappoint this week. Jeanty, who was out touched by Mike Washington Jr in the second half last week, faces the Los Angeles Rams who have allowed just two touchdowns to running backs. Hubbard faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who have allowed the second-fewest rushing yards per game, just two rushing touchdowns and the fifth-fewest fantasy PPG.
Cam Skattebo did not have a touch in Week 6. I do think he will earn touches back, but it is likely he is in a split at best. The New York Giants could opt to use three backs. Regardless, it is a tough matchup against the Houston Texans who have allowed the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs. Sit him for Woody Marks, J.K. Dobbins, Ollie Gordon II and even Dameon Pierce.
Sit Tony Pollard against the Cleveland Browns. He has seen volume on the ground, but has only two targets and no catches in the past two games. He is more of a floor play and floors are lowered in tough matchups. The Browns have allowed just one rush touchdown and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.
Unfortunately, my guy TreVeyon Henderson should be sat against the Bears, who have allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy PPG to RBs. The New England Patriots could be using three backs once again. Henderson also is dealing with an ankle injury that could hurt his explosiveness, which is his best attribute.
Get away from the Indianapolis Colts' pass catchers this week. The Vikings have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy PPG to wide receivers, including just three touchdowns against four interceptions on passes to the position. They have allowed the second-fewest fantasy PPG and no touchdowns to tight ends. Fantasy managers should try to get away from Tyler Warren, who is not a lock to play due to injury. They should certainly sit Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

George Pickens on practice report
By Todd Archer, NFL Nation Cowboys reporter

George Pickens was limited in Thursday's practice with a shoulder injury. He has been spotted after the last two games with ice on his shoulder after taking a hard fall on a catch in Week 5 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but this was the first time he was on the practice report. The issue is not expected to keep him out of Monday's game against the Eagles.

Oct. 21: J.J. McCarthy named Giants' starting QB for Week 7

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The inevitable has finally arrived in New York: McCarthy is reportedly going to start at quarterback for the Giants in Week 7.

It was a decision destined to happen at some point following McCarthy's Sept. 28 acquisition from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick. And it was a decision almost assuredly destined to happen this week after the Michigan product delivered 16.52 fantasy points in the fourth quarter alone, nearly leading his Giants to a comeback from down 34-10 to the Saints.

McCarthy's installation doesn't promise any miracles, not for the Giants and not for fantasy, but it's an understandable, aggressive move that could positively shift the team's offensive dynamic.

First off, don't take McCarthy's Week 6 performance remotely to heart, as it's almost entirely meaningless for evaluative purposes. High-scoring relief efforts by quarterbacks aren't uncommon. Since 2021, there have been 13 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who made a start later in that season; that group averaged 5.2 fewer fantasy points as starters than in that relief appearance.

More relevant to McCarthy's cause is his extensive tape from his 10 mediocre (to say it gently) starts in Minnesota last season. In those starts, he was 28th in Total QBR (36.1), 30th in completion rate (57.6%), 28th in off-target rate (19.3%) and 30th in touchdown-to-interception ratio (0.9). He struggled mightily when throwing into crowded spaces, with the fourth-worst passer rating when targeting a receiver with three or fewer yards of separation, per Next Gen Stats.

What McCarthy did do that could have fantasy relevance, however, was aim deep about as often as any quarterback in the league. His average depth of target of 8.8 yards led all quarterbacks who started at least half of their teams' games, though he did have seven interceptions on throws of at least 15 yards, putting his skill set into the extreme risk/reward category. Anyone who watched Sunday's game can attest to that, as McCarthy was chucking the ball in a desperate attempt to breathe some life into a Giants offense that, to that point, had shown barely any.

Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely each scored more than half of their Week 6 fantasy points after McCarthy entered the game, and the two combined for five catches on six targets for 130 yards and a touchdown on throws of at least 10 yards from McCarthy. Simply put, the upside is higher for both receivers with McCarthy under center, and that's especially relevant in a week with four teams on bye and the Giants facing an actually strong matchup against the Houston Texans defense. It's the fifth-most favorable matchup for wide receivers, when adjusted for the schedule.

Beyond those occasional highlight moments, also expect some ugly days for McCarthy, Nabers, Likely and anyone from the Giants' offense, depending on the quarterback's play, the matchups themselves and the current state of the running game. Cam Skattebo's last-minute role reduction (six snaps, no touches) thrust the offense into chaos last week, so we'll see how that plays out this week.

I've got McCarthy as my No. 21 quarterback in Week 7, which is a borderline superflex/2QB starter, though his upside could make him a stronger situational option than, say, Kirk Cousins against the Los Angeles Rams, if your lineup demands that.

Adonai Mitchell returns to Jets practice

By Rich Cimini, NFL Nation Jets Reporter

The Jets' WR, sidelined the last four games with an injured finger on his right hand, returned to practice Wednesday on a limited basis -- his first practice since Sept. 25. His availability for Sunday against the Dolphins is a "pain tolerance issue," according to head coach Aaron Glenn. During the brief media period at practice, Mitchell seemed reluctant to use his right hand on one pass play in particular. If he's active for the game, he'd probably join Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. in three-receiver sets.

Oct. 21: Are TEs more productive on National Tight Ends Day?

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

A note to Brock Bowers, Sam LaPorta, Juwan Johnson and all fellow tight ends: On Sunday, stand up and celebrate! It's National Tight Ends Day!

To their fantasy managers: You can all sit down. There's not much to see here.

Formally adopted as an NFL "holiday" beginning in 2019, National Tight Ends Day occurs on the fourth Sunday of October, as a way of honoring the position. This year, there is a 12-game slate on that day. Surely there'll be additional attention to the position on the highlight reel. For example, last season, Tucker Kraft and George Kittle celebrated their day with touchdowns, bringing it additional attention.

But from a fantasy perspective, historically speaking, National Tight Ends Day doesn't specifically inflate tight ends' production, at least not to decidedly actionable levels.

In the past seven seasons it has been celebrated (2019-25), tight end production was up only 0.29 fantasy points per game on October's fourth Sunday relative to the rest of the season, a differential as easily explained by random variance as by any additional boost provided by the now-annual event. Additionally, tight end usage was nearly identical to the numbers across the rest of the season, from routes run to target rate to red zone target rate to touchdowns scored.

There's only one area where a benefit seems apparent recently. Across the past three seasons, tight ends rostered in more than half of ESPN leagues at the time of National Tight Ends Day saw a boost of 3.65 fantasy points per game relative to the rest of their seasons. This was almost entirely due to the group seeing a noticeable, 17% boost in red zone target production, resulting in their touchdown rates more than doubling (0.66 per game, compared to 0.31 the rest of the season).

The small sample caveat naturally applies, since this was a group of 38 tight ends across three seasons. Additionally, across that same group, only three of their 40 best single-game totals from 2023-25 came on National Tight Ends Day. Is it possible that prominent tight ends are experiencing increasingly greater usage and attention on National Tight Ends Day as the holiday gains exposure across the league? Perhaps, and it's certainly something we're monitoring.

Is it something we should account for in our fantasy lineup planning? Well, no, not necessarily.

That said, if you're more moved by the data points, or if you're facing a razor-thin call at your flex spot between a tight end and a slightly more favorably projected running back or wide receiver, leaning tight end isn't an outrageous idea. Starting Mark Andrews (projected for 8.8 fantasy points in a favorable matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals) over Rome Odunze (projected for 10.2 in a less-ideal matchup against the New England Patriots) is a defensible move. Perhaps Lamar Jackson -- or Tyler Huntley, if Jackson is again out for Week 7 -- might choose to "celebrate" the occasion by giving Andrews that one additional red zone look he needs to hit paydirt.

Aside from that, sit back, enjoy the day, and here's hoping we see a third straight 20-point Isaiah Likely game and continued fantasy TE1 production from Kyle Pitts Sr., regardless of what the calendar tells us!

Oct. 20: Need RB help? Coleman set to return from IR this week

By Jeff Legwold, NFL Nation Broncos reporter

It will pay to keep an eye on the transactions this week, as the Denver Broncos are expected to activate rookie RB Jonah Coleman (19.8% rostered in ESPN leagues) from injured reserve. Coleman was the back of choice when the Broncos wanted to close out their Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, the same game in which he injured an ankle. Coleman has just the kind of decisiveness with the ball the Broncos need in the their run game right now. He will get some red zone carries because of his ability to break tackles, and he's a quality pass protector, so he'll get third-down snaps, as well.

Oct. 20: McLaurin, Evans leave MNF with injuries

By Michael F. Florio

Injuries were, unfortunately, the main story on Monday night. Terry McLaurin left early in the game as a result of a knee injury. He had to be carted off the field wearing an air cast. He seems likely to miss significant time. Mike Evans exited late in the first half -- after recording three catches for 94 yards -- due to an Achilles injury. Evans had been playing through this injury for the last couple of weeks. It seems likely he'll miss some time to allow this injury to heal.

The Evans injury led to more volume for the 49ers' stars. Both Christian McCaffrey (10) and George Kittle (8) had a season-high in targets. Both were already weekly must-starts but this added volume means even more production in fantasy.
Even without McLaurin, Jayden Daniels remains a weekly must-start. One week after running for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, he threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns. He has now scored at least 19 fantasy points in 17 out of his 22 career full games (77%). One thing to watch, however? He's been sacked nine times over the last two weeks.
Stefon Diggs saw seven targets on Monday night, going for 44 yards and a touchdown. He should see a boost in both targets and fantasy value as the top option for Daniels.
Chig Okonkwo is worth adding off the waiver wire for those streaming tight end. He saw seven targets, catching all of them for 69 yards. He led the Commanders in both catches and yards. His targets have increased each game this season and he may just be the No. 2 target for Daniels moving forward.
Treylon Burks left the game late. The Commanders are banged up at WR, meaning more volume could also go the way of Antonio Williams. Williams is worth a flier in 12-team leagues or deeper.
Rachaad White played on 71% of snaps, with seven carries and five targets. He turned that into 57 yards, a touchdown and 15.7 fantasy points. He is in play as an RB2 or flex option weekly with Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR.
After averaging 27.0 fantasy PPG over the season's first three weeks, Brock Purdy has cooled off averaging just 17.7 FPPG over the last three weeks. He still has been an extremely safe option and gets a bounceback opportunity next week against the Atlanta Falcons, who have allowed the third-most passing yards.

Time to cut your Chargers?

So, you drafted a Charger and are not sure what to do with them heading into the team's bye week?

Many of them are droppable, starting with Justin Herbert. He has not reached 14 fantasy points in any game this season and is currently the overall QB25. Numerous QBs who have missed multiple games (Lamar Jackson, Daniels, Michael Penix Jr) have scored more fantasy points that Herbert. The only place I wouldn't let him go is in a superflex league, where all starting QBs are rostered.

The toughest decision is with Omarion Hampton. He's a talented back with double-digit touches in every game. It's hard to give up on this kind of player. The issue is that the Chargers are splitting their snaps in thirds between their three RBs. The Chargers' interior offensive line is struggling to create running lanes and the offense, as a whole, is struggling to create consistent scoring opportunities.

I have a lot of shares of Hampton but, as tempting as it has been, I have not yet dropped him. In 12-team leagues or deeper, you have no choice but to hold on. In 10-team leagues, it comes down to your RB depth. I played Rachaad White over Hampton in one league this week, which is making me question why I haven't dropped him. Still, after looking over the waiver wire, there's simply more upside in holding onto Hampton.

Ladd McConkey is the other question. McConkey has been extremely banged up and has left early in all but one game this season. I still believe in the talent -- and the bye week should (hopefully) allow him to get healthy. Please? I'm not ready to give up on McConkey and would keep him. However, the rest of the Chargers can be dropped if you're in need of finding a bye week replacement.

Of course, in most leagues, waivers don't run until early Wednesday morning. Spend today trying to trade any of these guys in exchange for a player you may like more than what's available on the waiver wire. Who knows? There may just be a manager in your league who still believes in a big name like Herbert.

Oct. 19: How Davante Adams injury affects Rams offense

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The news on Davante Adams' injury suffered Sunday is devastating, as Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday that the veteran wide receiver has a ruptured hamstring and will miss 6 to 10 weeks. Adams is the No. 7 wide receiver in fantasy points (102.0, or 17.0 per game), and he had been a top-10 weekly scorer in three of his first five games.

A 6-to-10 week timetable effectively ends Adams' fantasy regular season, as the midpoint of that range would take us through Week 14, directly before standard league playoffs begin. Though most leagues offer IR spots in which he could be stashed, steering through the bye weeks while keeping him there -- even if you're granted two or more of them -- isn't easy to do. If you need roster flexibility for bye weeks or injury fill-ins, it's reasonable to drop Adams in order to seek replacements. For now, try to keep him stashed there once he's officially moved to injured reserve, considering his past production and fantasy playoffs utility. The Rams have an extremely favorable Week 15 matchup for the position (DAL), as one example.

In Adams' absence, the Rams' offense takes a noticeable hit, as Adams and fellow Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had accounted for 42% of the team's total targets for the season, and that's despite Nacua having missed two games due to a groin injury. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington will all likely see expanded roles while Adams is out, with Mumpfied the closest to fantasy relevant and more so in 12-team leagues with deep benches or 14-plus-team formats. Be aware, however, that those three totaled 12 targets and 24.4 fantasy points during Nacua's Weeks 2-3 absences, reflecting their low priority in the receiving pecking order.

It's the Rams' tight ends who should benefit most while Adams heals, as was the case in those same Weeks 2-3 games. Terrance Ferguson scored 17.4 fantasy points on nine targets in Week 2, before injuring his MCL in Week 3 and landing on IR. Tyler Higbee emerged with 20.2 fantasy points on 11 targets in Week 3, and he has now averaged 12.4 points and 6.8 targets in the past four weeks. Higbee is a definite add in any league larger than ESPN's standard, and Ferguson, who is eligible to return in Week 8, could warrant similar appeal if he's ready to play a week from now.

Stafford, meanwhile, will probably be more matchup dependent while Adams is sidelined. The veteran quarterback has been hit-or-miss for much of the season to date, but he'd offer his best fantasy utility for what align as favorable matchups in Weeks 9 (WSH), 10 (@ARI) and 15 (DAL).

stories.headline: Pistons C Jalen Duren out at least two weeks with hamstring strain
stories.summary: Pistons center Jalen Duren, who signed a five-year extension earlier this month, will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain.
stories.body:
Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday.

Duren suffered the injury in the first half of Friday's win over the Miami Heat. He played only 10 minutes before leaving the game.

"It's tough when you lose a guy that means as much to us as JD does," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before Sunday's game in Philadelphia. "It's tough. Tough for him. Trying to come back and get himself situated to start the year. You miss those days. It's obviously a little bit difficult for us."

Duren's offseason was marked by a lengthy standoff with the Pistons over a contract extension. He missed media day and the first few practices of training camp before ultimately signing a five-year, $200 million deal.

Last season, he averaged a career high in points (19.5 PPG), made his first All-Star team and was named to the All-NBA third team as the Pistons earned the top seed in the Eastern Conference. But he struggled mightily in the postseason, dropping to 10.2 points per game in 14 playoff games before Detroit's second-round exit.

Duren scored 22 points with nine rebounds in Detroit's season-opening win over the Boston Celtics.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.
